scope: Python client close-failure diagnostics and contract integration; no engine protocol, gameplay ABI, build or GPU change.

api.value: Most recent TransportError raised by close, or None before any such failure.
api.retention: A later successful close does not clear the retained error; a later close TransportError replaces it.
api.primary_exception: Context cleanup preserves an active body exception without attaching attributes or printing diagnostics.
limits: The property is not process-liveness or process-closure evidence.
Exceptions may contain paths or transport diagnostics; callers choose what to record.
Close and context-manager error propagation otherwise remain unchanged.

linux_integrated_without_native.reason_for_skips: No engine was selected; all six NativeContract cases explicitly skipped.

diagnostic_tests.scope: In-memory failures and mocked process/thread construction exercise the real client and transport context/close paths. Tests do not launch a process or thread.
coverage: No previous error and read-only property
Failed close retains exact error object
Body exception remains identical, including foreign exceptions rejecting attribute assignment
Interrupts are not swallowed by ordinary close

compatibility.syntax_check: Python 3.9 grammar accepted for successor SDK and diagnostic test.
compatibility.existing_ctest_registration: python_client_contract discovers CleanupDiagnostics via its main fixture; no new CMake registration.

limits: Results qualify the exact isolated SDK implementation, documentation and tests identified above, against native 0.0.134 on both platforms.
The test tree retains SDK metadata 0.0.138; publication metadata 0.0.140 does not change the qualified implementation bytes. No newly compiled engine or installed distribution is claimed.

The thirteen diagnostic tests use controlled in-memory errors and mocked process/thread construction; the complete suite also runs real synthetic subprocess peers and six native authoring contract tests.
